 Feast or famine
 Busy on the tools, invisible for the jobs you want 
 1 The work you get now
 Your work comes from word of mouth and the odd directory, and it is feast or famine. Your site, if you have one, does not show the jobs you actually want more of, and you are on the tools when the phone rings.
 2 Not in the running
 Customers searching for an EICR or an EV charger install pick from the electricians Google shows them. If your site does not have a page for that job in their area, you are not in the running. Each missed call while you are on site is a job the next sparky picks up.
 3 The work you want next
 A page for each job you want, in each area you cover, with your registration on show and a quote form that works on a phone. Add the AI receptionist and nothing goes to voicemail again.

 How a job list becomes a site
 Tell Andy the jobs, he builds the pages 
 01 Write down the work you want
 Domestic rewires, landlord EICRs, commercial fit-outs: name the jobs you would take more of, and the areas you will drive to.
 02 Each job gets a page
 Andy writes and builds them from your service list, scheme numbers and photos, then shows you the preview.
 03 Live, with a form that asks which job
 On your own domain, set up for Google, with quotes arriving in your inbox when you are between sites.

 A field engineer first
 Andy knows what a day on the road involves 
 Before Antek Automation, Andy was a field engineer who became a service manager, over 30 years in field service and managed print. His background is field service rather than electrical contracting, but call-outs, missed calls and paperwork in the van are familiar ground.
 Websites for electricians are built around how the trade gets booked. You supply the service list, registration details and job photos, and Andy does the rest from his office in Andover.

 Questions from the trade
 What electricians ask before committing 
 Do you understand electrical work?
 Andy's background is field service, not electrical contracting, and he will not pretend otherwise. Over 30 years of it means he knows how reactive work runs. The technical content comes from what you supply: your service list, scheme numbers and photos.
 Can you show my NICEIC or NAPIT badge?
 Yes, your own, shown with your registration details once you confirm them. Antek Automation only displays a badge a client actually holds.
 I get work from a lead site already. Why my own site?
 Leads from a lead site are rented: you pay for them, and the customer may well be sent to other firms too. Enquiries from your own site are yours, and you keep the page that won them.
 Can it take emergency calls out of hours?
 Yes, with the AI receptionist, which is set up from £497 and runs from £97 a month. It answers in your business name day and night, takes the details and books or passes them on. AI voice agents for electricians covers it in depth.
 How much does an electrician website cost?
 Starter at £600 suits a sole trader with a tight list of jobs, and Core at £995 suits a firm with more to show. Extra job pages are £125, and hosting and care is £10 a month.
 How long until my job pages are live?
 Allow 1 to 3 weeks from your deposit. Scheme details and photos of real installs are normally what holds a build up, so have them to hand.
 If I sell the business, does the website go with it?
 You own the site once it is paid for. It can be passed on along with the rest of the firm's assets.
 Do you build for other trades?
 This site is only for electricians. Plumbers should look at plumberwebdesign.co.uk , and other trades at web design for tradespeople .
 A page for every job you want more of.

Who builds your job pages
 Andy Norman, building sites around the jobs you want 
 Thirty-plus years in field service and managed print took Andy from field engineer to service manager. Antek Automation came after that, and it is where he builds websites for trades and local firms.
 He is plain about the limits. His background is field service, not electrical contracting, and any scheme badge on a site he builds belongs to the electrician whose site it is.
 Why the job list comes first
 Field service runs on knowing exactly which job is next and where. A website for an electrician should work the same way, with a page for each kind of work so a customer can find the one they need.

## https://electricianwebdesign.co.uk/seo-for-electricians

SEO for electricians
 SEO for electricians, measured area by area 
 Electrician SEO is £497 a month for domestic and commercial electricians who already have a Google profile. It covers the map results, reviews and profile upkeep that decide who gets found nearby.
 Marketing for electricians is often sold as bought-in leads. This is different: you build up your own presence, and nobody sells your enquiries to anyone else.
 What is included each month
 One fixed scope, whichever areas you cover.
 A monthly LocalFalcon map-rank report across the areas you cover
 Review requests and replies through the CRM
 Scheduled Google profile posts
 Google profile upkeep
 A monthly summary
 How results are shown
 Each report is a LocalFalcon grid across your patch, showing where you appear on the map point by point. Move from one month to the next and you can see which areas have shifted.
 What is not included
 No ranking guarantees, no lead selling and no ads. Link building and suspension recovery are also outside it, and citations clean-up is an add-on priced per job. For calls you cannot get to, AI for electricians covers missed-call answering, and Antek's core website service covers the build.

## https://electricianwebdesign.co.uk/features

What goes on the site
 What goes into an electrician website 
 A proper electrician website has one page per job, your scheme badges, the areas you cover, a way to reach you in an emergency and a form that asks which job is needed.
 Anyone searching for an electrician website template usually wants this list. The difference is that Andy builds it for you, so there is no template left to fill in. The same goes for an electrical contractor website, with the commercial work brought forward.
 Which service pages should an electrician have?
 One for each job you want more of. Starter gives you five pages in total, Core gives you eight, and any page beyond that is £125.
 Rewires
 Consumer unit upgrades
 EICRs
 Fault finding
 EV charger installs
 Solar and battery, if you offer it
 Commercial work
 How are scheme badges handled?
 Your NICEIC, NAPIT or other membership badge is supplied by you and shown with your details. Antek Automation never claims a membership on a client's behalf, and only shows what you confirm.
 How do areas covered work?
 You say how far you will travel, and the towns you name are set out on the site so customers and Google both know where you work.
 What is the emergency call-out block?
 A prominent section with your number, for people with no power and no patience. If you want it answered when you cannot pick up, the AI receptionist can do that.
 What does the quote form ask?
 Name, number, and the job type, so you can tell an EV charger enquiry from a fault before you ring back. It works on a phone and sends to your inbox.
 What about reviews and Google?
 A reviews block shows your own customers' words. You also get guidance on setting up your Google profile, which matters as much as the site. For the wider picture, see Antek's web design service .
